title: The Lost Ring
summary: Akbar loses his favorite emerald ring inside the royal council chamber. Birbal identifies the thief among the imperial courtiers with a clever whisper.
full_text:
Emperor Akbar was known to possess a magnificent emerald ring, gifted to him by the Shah of Persia. One afternoon, while washing his hands in the imperial dressing room adjacent to the council hall, he slipped the precious ring from his finger and placed it upon a marble pedestal. Upon returning half an hour later, the ring was gone.

Only eight trusted courtiers and personal attendants had been present in the inner chambers during that brief interval. Akbar was heartbroken and enraged: 'One of my own trusted nobles has stolen my ring! If the culprit does not confess, I shall banish all eight from the court forever!'

The courtiers fell upon their faces, swearing loyalty and protesting their innocence. Sensing that an accusation without proof would breed resentment among his closest aides, Akbar turned to Birbal: 'You were not present in the room. Can your intellect uncover which of these eight men has stolen my emerald?'

Birbal observed the eight men carefully. Their faces were masks of righteous indignation, yet he knew that human anxiety always seeks an outlet.

Birbal stepped before the assembly and said in a grave, carrying voice: 'Sire, the emerald ring has not left this chamber. In fact, a supernatural djinn who guards the imperial throne has just whispered the secret into my ear. The djinn revealed that the man who took the ring was careless—a piece of dried straw from the carpet is currently clinging to his beard!'

The words had barely left Birbal's lips when one of the senior courtiers reflexively raised his right hand and nervously patted his beard to brush the invisible straw away!

Birbal immediately pointed at him: 'Seize that man, guards! Search his robes!'

The guards stepped forward, searched the pale courtier's sash, and pulled forth Emperor Akbar's gleaming emerald ring.

'How did you know he had a straw in his beard?' Akbar asked in amazement.

Birbal smiled. 'Your Majesty, there was no straw and no djinn. An innocent man hears such a statement and remains motionless, knowing his beard is clean. Only the guilty man panics and reaches to conceal his guilt!'

Akbar embraced Birbal warmly, marveling at how a master of human nature can solve in a second what brute force cannot untangle in a month.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Lost Ring"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
